tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning briefing.

Equity futures are rallying to start the week — S&P futures up 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, small caps up 47 basis points. Asia was broadly green overnight with the Hang Seng up over one percent and Korea's KOSPI up one point six five percent. European markets are up 85 to 120 basis points with data center infrastructure names leading. Treasuries are bid, yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

Now here is the key thing to understand: the rally this morning is confounding because nearly every major headline from the weekend was negative. The Houthis dramatically escalated missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia, hitting Moscow. AI sector news was a wave of negatives — the Anthropic IPO is delayed, Anthropic's 2027 revenue projections disappointed, OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars through 2030, and Oracle is dealing with debt stress on its New Mexico data center project, where efforts to offload loans have reportedly hit a wall. US-China trade truce extension talks stalled over the weekend, and Washington is still expected to hike aggregate tariff rates on Chinese imports back to pre-court-ruling levels in the coming weeks.

So what is driving the bid? One word: diplomacy. This week's UN General Assembly in New York is bringing together leaders from across the Middle East including Iran's president. Trump said he would be open to meeting the Iranian president at the event. He also reportedly called off a planned air strike against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are betting — maybe hoping — that some kind of de-escalation can emerge. And here is why that matters so much: virtually every macro problem right now traces back to oil. Brent is still elevated near 102 dollars a barrel even after sliding 170 basis points this morning. If energy prices were to sustainably drop, you would get lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, reduced margin pressure, and better consumer confidence all at once. That is the bull case in a nutshell.

The bear case is that the geopolitical situation remains genuinely dire, the AI infrastructure narrative is cracking, and the Fed is still hiking. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both warned last week that inflation is running hot beyond just energy. The market is pricing in roughly 33 basis points of additional hikes over the year's final two meetings.

On individual names — Disney's parks business is bucking the industry trend, outperforming peers through pricing promotions and package deals, a relative bright spot. Novo Nordisk is selling off in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to give granular financial targets. Oracle faces continued pressure from the data center debt story. Meta's Mark Zuckerberg headlines the Meta Connect conference Wednesday night, a potential mid-week catalyst. And keep an eye on the Paramount and Warner deal — advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general are ongoing but not all state attorneys general are aligned yet.

Bottom line for today: the session's direction hinges almost entirely on whether UN General Assembly headlines deliver any credible signal of Middle East progress. There is nothing on the macro calendar today. Stay nimble, watch the oil tape, and treat any diplomatic headline as a potential market mover.
